label: Alpha Geometry, Tsallis Entropy, and SPD Matrices
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 71 through 106. One change of coordinates, the alpha representation, makes positive measures dually flat and unifies alpha geodesics, Tsallis q-entropy, escort distributions, and log-det divergences on positive-definite matrices. We will watch extra geometric room appear on the cone and track what survives back on probabilities.

label: The Alpha Representation
notes: For a positive measure, the alpha representation raises each coordinate to the power one minus alpha over two, with a logarithmic limit at alpha equal to one. Its dual is the minus-alpha representation. On the positive cone these power coordinates straighten a Bregman geometry, giving a whole alpha family of dually flat structures rather than a single one.

label: Why Simplex Geodesics Bend
notes: On the positive cone an alpha geodesic is a straight segment in alpha coordinates. On the simplex we draw the same segment but must renormalize, so the curve bends. The visible bend changes with alpha because a flat connection upstairs meets the curved normalization constraint downstairs, leaving only limiting mixture and exponential cases affine.

label: Alpha Divergence and Pythagoras
notes: The alpha divergence reads as a Bregman divergence in alpha coordinates. At alpha equal to zero the square-root coordinate makes it a constant times squared Euclidean distance, so orthogonality gives a literal Pythagorean identity. The notebook verifies this on a small example, with the identity error coming out exactly zero.

label: Alpha Means Interpolate Averages
notes: The weighted alpha mean averages values in the alpha representation and inverts back. As alpha sweeps the interval, the mean slides continuously between the arithmetic average at one endpoint and the geometric average at the logarithmic limit. This single tunable knob recovers the familiar Pythagorean family of means as special cases.

label: Tsallis q-Entropy
notes: Tsallis q-entropy deforms Shannon entropy with a q-logarithm and approaches it as q tends to one. The chapter ties the deformation to alpha geometry through the dictionary alpha equals two q minus one. The deformed power coordinate flattens differently near the simplex boundary, which is why q-entropy optimization can emphasize rare or dominant events.

label: Escort Distributions
notes: The q-escort distribution raises each probability to the power q and renormalizes. For q above one large coordinates are amplified; for q below one small coordinates gain relative mass. Escorts are not ad hoc smoothing weights but coordinates of a second dual-flat construction, with a metric conformally related to the invariant geometry in the special case.

label: Lab: Alpha Integration of Experts
notes: Alpha integration pools expert categorical predictions linearly in alpha coordinates, then normalizes. Negative alpha behaves like mixture pooling, positive alpha like multiplicative exponential pooling, and intermediate values tune the compromise. Scoring the pooled prediction against a held-out target by alpha divergence selects the best representation, here near alpha equal to minus one.

label: SPD Matrices and Log-Det Divergence
notes: A positive-definite matrix extends a positive measure from diagonal entries to full spectra and orientations. The Stein or log-det divergence uses trace of P Q-inverse minus log determinant minus n. It is nonnegative, zero only when the matrices coincide, and invariant under congruence transformations by any invertible A acting on both arguments.

label: Geometry of the SPD Cone
notes: Positive-definite matrices form an open convex cone whose boundary is the loss of positive definiteness. The log-det divergence rises steeply toward that wall, as the contour landscape around the identity shows. Congruence invariance is the matrix analogue of changing coordinates, mirroring how alpha representations rescale positive measures while preserving geometric content.

label: Synthesis and Pitfalls
notes: Three coordinate choices organize the chapter: alpha representations flatten the cone, the simplex bends most of them, and escorts plus SPD matrices generalize the idea. Common pitfalls are treating q and alpha as unrelated, forgetting renormalization inside the simplex, and assuming every invariant divergence is flat when the log-det family includes both.
